cap: Precocious puberty means signs before 8 years in girls or 9 years in boys, and LH sorts it. A pubertal LH means the whole axis woke early: central precocious puberty, treated with a continuous GnRH agonist such as depot leuprolide. A suppressed LH means sex steroids come from outside the axis, as in McCune-Albright syndrome, an activating GNAS mutation. A prepubertal LH with near-normal bone age and no growth spurt points to a benign variant.
teach: A basal LH above roughly 0.3 mIU/mL on an ultrasensitive assay, or a peak above roughly 5 mIU/mL after GnRH stimulation, shows central puberty. In a boy, both testes of 4 mL or more with a pubertal LH point to the central axis, one enlarged testis suggests a Leydig cell tumor, and virilization with small testes suggests the adrenal glands or exogenous androgen. Familial testotoxicosis is an activating LH receptor mutation that makes Leydig cells secrete testosterone without LH. A peripheral cause that goes on long enough can advance the bone age and switch the central axis on.
